title: Mud End — the peat hamlet three leagues downriver of Sill
caption: The peat hamlet three leagues downriver of Sill, drawn at walking scale on the dry shelf above the marsh: nine houses and their peat stacks, the byre where the moot meets and its moot-post, sods set out to dry, the peat cuttings in the southern banks, and a landing and punt on the Ilm. The Clay Road runs west to Sill and east the fifteen leagues on to Greybank, both drawn faint at the edges for neighbourhood only; the marsh drain comes down into the river, and Reedholt stands faint among the reeds to the south. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Grain, with compass, a league scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the winter peat that decides who stays warm, the man taken quiet in his sleep and called merciful, and the wolves of Reedholt. An engraved peat spade sits in the margin.
